title.narrative: Towards ending HIV as a public health threat by 2030 - Zimbabwe (01-Jan-2024-31-Dec-2026)

description.narrative: Zimbabwe, HIV, United Nations Development Programme (UNDP Zimbabwe)This program has the following goals: To accelerate the country's response towards ending AIDS as a public health problem in Zimbabwe by 2030. To reduce HIV incidence in Zimbabwe by 60% from 0.48% in 2018 to less than 0.19% by 2026. To reduce AIDS-related deaths in Zimbabwe by 60% from 21,800 in 2018 to less than 10,464 in 2026. The objectives of this program are: 95 % of people on treatment in all regions, age groups, genders, and population groups have suppressed Viral Load. 95 % of PLHIV in all regions and among all populations know their status. 95 % PLHIV in all regions, age groups, genders, and population groups have increased access to screening, prevention, management and treatment for HIV including TB, NCDs, STIs, Hepatitis. At least 95% of AGYW receive a defined package of HIV and SRH services by 2026. To achieve and sustain elimination of mother to child transmission of HIV, hepatitis and syphilis by 2026. To increase condom use among high risk males and females during risky sexual encounters to at least 90% by 2026. To reach 90% of those sexually active reached with STI diagnosis, management and treatment
